text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA
- Yugoslavia has greatly contibuted to the allies' battle against fascism in WWII, said Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic when receiving Yugoslav WWII veterans on occasion of V-day.

- Slovenian Foreign Ministry official Ivo Vajgl denied reports in Belgrade press that Yugoslavia and Slovenia would establish diplomatic relations this month but did not rule out closer ties between the two countries.

- Yugoslavia's Post and Telecommunications are soon to be separated into two units of which the post alone would employ 16,700 of the total of some 30,000 workers, says deputy general manager Milan Brujic.
- Economists are called on to prescribe a therapy not only give a diagnosis, says Serbian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister Coordinator Dragan Tomic at an economists meeting in Nis.
- Yugoslav exporters have to take stock of EU anti-dumping measures in force when they return to EU markets, said Yugoslav Foreign Trade Minister Biorislav Vukovic.
- New Serbian Interior Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic visits Belgrade police.

- Upcoming elections will be historic in many ways and the Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) has very good prospects because the opposition has shown it is incapable of ruling, said member of the SPS Main Board Zeljko Simic.
- Yugoslavia's main goal should be EU membership and seeking associate membership is the first step in this direction, says New Democracy vice-president Radivoje Lazarevic.
- Kosovo Albanian leader Ibrahim Rugova postponed elections for the Kosovo parallel parliament to Decmeber 24.
NASA BORBA
- Socialist Party of Serbia seems to be pushing aside its reformist option and taking over its nationalist one ahead of the republican elections, paper's sources say.
- The Democratic Party allows possibility of new parties joinining coalition Zajedno into an assymetric coaliton.
- The regime is preparing conflicts in Kosovo to mobilise Serbs ahead of elections and push democratic processes into the background, says spokesman of the Civic Alliance Goran Svilanovic.

- Modernisation and reforms are a must for Serbia and the question is not who will win at the coming elections but who is able to move the country ahead, says Democratic Party President Zoran Djindjic.
- Zastava trucks from Kragujevac and Italy's Iveco agree to continue coooperation in their joint venture Zastava-Iveco in which the Itallian firm has a 46 percent stake.
- Interest rate on the free market could drop to below three percent a month by the end of the year from present 10-12 percent, said National Bank of Yugoslavia Vice-Governor Ratko Banovic.
POLITIKA EKSPRES

- Serbian education minister sacks his deputy Vojislav Braunovic for travelling on a trip to Mexico without authorisation. The trip which grouped a number of school directors was much criticised by the media.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- Some 100,000 second-hand cars were imported in Yugoslavia using a loophole in the federal law. Cars imported via Bosnian Serb Republic or eastern Slavonia cost the state coffres about 100 millon German marks in customs duties.
- MONTENEGRO -
POBJEDA
- Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic is on a visit to Britain to May 9 where he will meet Tony Lloyd the newly appointed minister in the Foreign Office in charge of Central and South East Europe.

- Montenegro has seriously progressed towards a free society governed by high standards of freedom, rule of law and humanity, said parliament speaker Svetozar Marovic opening an international seminar on British political philosopher Karl Popper.
- The second International Festival of Alternative Theatre (FIAT) costs 250,000 German marks. It will be opened Friday by Helen Steward, founder of New York's La Mamma theatre.
MONITOR

- President Momir Bulatovic will not call for a confidence vote in Milo Djukanovic's government because the government will survive if only ten deputies of the Democratic Party of Socialists support the prime minister, editorial.

- Montenegro's business with tobacco and second-car smuggling from Herzegovina comes to an end. Serbian authorities put Nis airport in full operation for smuggling. The recent visit of Moldavian Prime Minister confirms new tobacco routes Kisenyev-Nis.

- Montenegro got statistically 15,000-20,000 new citizens in the last two months according to moderate estimates. Serbian citizens fictitiously changed their addresses in order to import second-hand cars from Bosnia under low Montenegrin taxes. -- Belgrade newsroom + 381 11 222 4305
